html_en:
A big day for AI product updates — Claude drops usage limits, Gemini lands on the iPhone Duo at launch, and a broader debate simmers about whether AI will wreck the economy or supercharge it.

Claude Goes Ultra: Anthropic Cleans Up Its Pricing (and Its Branding)

Anthropic made two moves today that power users have been waiting for. First, the company retired the awkward "Max 5x / Max 20x" naming in favor of something cleaner: Max ($100/month) and Ultra ($200/month). Second — and more importantly — it removed the five-hour usage cap that had been the bane of heavy Claude users on the top tier.

"We're removing the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts... Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until they're verified, which helps us prevent fraud and abuse." — @claudeai

The announcement (nearly 27,000 likes at time of writing) was one of the day's most-engaged posts. @bcherny confirmed the change with a terse post that racked up over 8,000 likes. Alex Albert offered his own editorial gloss:

"Ultra has a better ring to it than Max 20x. Also no more 5 hour rate limits for Ultra subs." — @alexalbert__

Weekly limits remain in place, so this isn't quite unlimited — but for the kind of users who were hitting the five-hour wall, it's a meaningful unlock. Meanwhile, @steipete used the moment to make a broader point about platform dependency, warning users that relying on any vendor means accepting their ability to change the rules at any time — a tension that's only going to grow as these tools become infrastructure.

Gemini and ryOS: The iPhone Duo Finds Its AI Companions

Apple's new iPhone Duo hardware is barely out and the AI ecosystem is already jockeying for position on it. Google moved fast.

"Last Friday, the iPhone Duo came out. @GeminiApp was there on day 1, optimized for it." — @joshwoodward

But the most visually striking reaction came from the indie side. @ryolu_ posted a demo of ryOS running on the iPhone Duo — a custom OS layer that generated over 1,100 likes and a chorus of TestFlight requests. The cheeky tagline: "better than iOS ☺️." It's exactly the kind of scrappy, imaginative response to new hardware that signals a healthy dev ecosystem forming around the device.

Separately, @thsottiaux teased upcoming multi-account switching on mobile — and hinted at something bigger coming in the next two days with a cryptic "👀."

The Agent Economy: From Self-Maintaining Software to Enterprise Guardrails

The race to make software agents actually useful — not just impressive in demos — dominated builder conversation today. Amjad Masad at Replit unveiled what he's calling Self-Maintaining Software:

"If you host your apps on Replit and enable 'autofix' it becomes Self-Maintaining Software." — @amasad

Replit also launched a Government edition and published a whitepaper on sandboxing agents safely — a sign that the company is pushing hard into regulated, risk-sensitive verticals where the stakes for an agent doing something unexpected are considerably higher than in consumer apps.

That exact tension — autonomy vs. control — sits at the heart of today's most substantive podcast. On No Priors, Jake Stauch, CEO of enterprise startup Serval, made the case that general-purpose AI agents fail in large organizations not because the AI is bad, but because enterprise permission structures are so constrained that even a brilliant agent can "barely read your emails."

"The agent becomes pretty competent. They could theoretically just start writing code that could take action on all your systems, and that is an unbounded security risk that I don't think anyone's gonna be able to take anytime soon." — Jake Stauch, Serval

Serval's pitch: be the guardrail layer that makes coding agents safe enough for IT departments — who can then pass the capability to HR, finance, and legal. It's a distinctly unsexy value proposition ("we are the guardrails") but potentially a very large business if it works. Watch/Listen: No Priors — Taking on ServiceNow: Coding Agents for the Rest of Us

The AGI Optimism Wars

Every day now brings a fresh skirmish in the debate over what advanced AI actually means for human economic life. Today's most-liked contribution came from @trq212, who argued that catastrophist framings are themselves a kind of failure of imagination:

"The solution to economic doomerism is to be even more AGI-pilled. I believe in a well-aligned ASI that can explain its work and bring us along, one that makes each individual maximally effective." — @trq212
"Basically everyone is bad at predicting how more intelligence will actually show up in the economy. And the simplest answer of 'it'll cost a lot and unemploy everyone' is actually not very AGI-pilled imo — we should avoid hyperstitioning it into reality." — @trq212

Guillermo Rauch kept it even simpler: "We're in humanity's golden age." Meanwhile, Matt Turck poured cold water on a viral story about France allegedly moving to regulate AI, noting that the vote involved "11 populist morons in the lower chamber" with 35 of 577 MPs present — "zero chance of becoming law," but "still embarrassing."

The optimism is easy to mock, but it's worth noting who's saying it: builders who are watching their tools improve in real time. Rauch noted that his AI systems are now "continuously benchmarking and asking it to improve its own performance" — self-improving infrastructure that was science fiction a couple of years ago. Whether that translates to broadly shared prosperity or concentrated gains remains the central unanswered question of the moment.
html_zh:
今天的主旋律是边界的消融——AI工具的使用限制在松动，企业级自动化的门槛在降低，而乐观主义者与悲观主义者之间关于AI经济影响的论战，也比任何时候都更加激烈。

🤖 Claude Ultra：告别五小时魔咒

本周最受瞩目的产品动态，来自Anthropic。@claudeai 官方宣布对订阅计划进行品牌重塑，并取消了备受诟病的使用限制：

"我们正在重命名 Max 计划：Max 5x → Max，Max 20x → Ultra。Max 依然 $100/月，Ultra 依然 $200。我们也正在为已验证的 Ultra 账户取消五小时使用限制，今天起对大多数现有订阅者生效。"
— @claudeai

这条推文获得了近 27,000 个点赞，是今日全场数据最高的一条。Anthropic 产品负责人 @bcherny 也单独确认了这一消息，而 @alexalbert__ 则补充道：

"Ultra 听起来比 Max 20x 顺耳多了。另外，Ultra 订阅者不再有五小时速率限制。"

值得注意的是，@steipete 对此表示认可，同时也借机提醒开发者：

"这很聪明。奇怪的是这不是默认设置。不可预测的推理质量通常是我建议绕过中间商的原因。"

同一天，Claude 还宣布即将支持移动端多账户切换功能，桌面端也即将跟进，构建者 @thsottiaux 在其连载"产品日志"第26天中透露了这一消息，并留下了耐人寻味的伏笔："接下来两天会有重置……储备……你们懂的 👀"。

📱 新硬件，新战场：iPhone Duo 首日争夺战

苹果发布 iPhone Duo 的同一天，各大 AI 应用纷纷亮出了自己的成绩单。Google 的 @joshwoodward 宣布：

"上周五，iPhone Duo 发布。@GeminiApp 在第一天就上线了，并专门为其进行了优化。"

而独立开发者 @ryolu_ 则用一种更叛逆的方式宣示存在——他将自己打造的 ryOS 运行在 iPhone Duo 上，并称其"比 iOS 还好用"，引发了超过 1,100 个点赞的关注。

🏢 企业级 AI 的"护城河"：Serval 的赌注

本期播客中，No Priors 访谈了 Serval 联合创始人兼 CEO Jake Stauch，他们聊的核心问题是：为什么面向普通员工的 AI Agent 在大企业里几乎无法落地？

Watch/Listen: Taking on ServiceNow: Coding Agents the Rest of Us — No Priors

Jake 的判断直击要害——企业里个人权限的天花板，才是个人 AI 助手的真正敌人：

"在大型企业里，有大量关于审批、关于你能做什么不能做什么的流程……你的个人权限受到极大限制，即使你被允许把自己的 Agent 带去工作——很多情况下你根本不被允许——它能做的事情也极其有限。它甚至几乎无法读取你的邮件。"
— Jake Stauch，Serval CEO

Serval 的解法是：以 IT 部门为切入点，用代码生成 Agent 替代 ServiceNow 的昂贵顾问模式，同时引入严格的确定性审批流程和审计追踪。Jake 将其定位为"面向普通人的代码 Agent"，让不懂编程的 IT、HR、法务团队也能成为构建者。

"Serval 就是那道边界，就是那道护栏。我们是让一个拥有大量规则、审批流程和政治博弈的大型企业，能够安全、舒适地大规模采用这些工具的方式。"

🌐 乐观主义作为一种战略

今天推特上还有一场低调但值得关注的思想交锋，主角是 @trq212，他对流行的"AI 经济末日论"发起了正面反驳：

"几乎所有人都不擅长预测更强的智能究竟会如何在经济中显现。而'它会花很多钱并让所有人失业'这个最简单的答案，在我看来其实并不是真正的 AGI 信徒该有的观点。我们应该避免把它变成现实。"
"对抗经济末日论的解药，是更彻底地相信 AGI。我相信一个对齐良好的 ASI——它能解释自己的工作，带着我们一起前进，让每个个体都能发挥最大的效能。"

Vercel CEO @rauchg 的一句话则以极简的方式呼应了这种情绪：

"我们正处于人类的黄金时代。"

当然，并非所有乐观都指向宏大叙事。Replit 创始人 @amasad 发布了"自我维护软件"功能——开启 autofix 后，托管在 Replit 上的应用可以自动检测并修复问题；同时还宣布了面向政府机构的 Replit for Government 产品线。黄金时代，或许真的已经悄悄开始了。
